items.headline: About 3 million adult Singaporeans to get final Assurance Package cash payout from December
items.summary: The Ministry of Finance says about 3 million citizens aged 21 and above will receive between S$100 and S$250 in the fifth and final tranche of the enhanced Assurance Package, with payouts beginning in December.

items.headline: LTA orders Grab to pause some Punggol self-driving tests after near-miss with schoolgirl
items.summary: The Land Transport Authority directed Grab to suspend autonomous-vehicle testing at certain junctions after a WeRide-made shuttle braked and swerved near a schoolgirl at a Punggol crossing on 5 November; an investigation is under way.

items.headline: Three new MRT stations — Bedok South, Sungei Bedok and Xilin — to open on 26 December
items.summary: The LTA will open Bedok South and Sungei Bedok on the Thomson-East Coast Line and Xilin on the Downtown Line on 26 December; Sungei Bedok becomes the second TEL-DTL interchange and completes the 29-station line.

items.headline: Singapore's car population cannot grow much further, Acting Transport Minister tells Parliament
items.summary: Acting Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow told Parliament that with about 660,000 passenger cars already using more than a tenth of Singapore's land, the car population has little room to expand, as the government studies a COE feebate favouring mass-market cars.

items.headline: New Delhi chokes in severe post-Diwali smog as firecrackers breach court limits
items.summary: Air quality across parts of Delhi reached the 'severe' band after Diwali, with readings many times the WHO daily limit, as residents set off firecrackers well beyond the Supreme Court's permitted green-cracker windows.

items.headline: India's wealthy pivot to real estate after two years of weak stock returns
items.summary: With equities delivering lacklustre returns, affluent Indians are shifting into property and logistics; Bloomberg reports at least six vehicles launched in 2026 are seeking to raise more than US$1.25 billion for such assets.

items.headline: IIFL Finance founder bets Blackstone deal will drive 25-30% annual lending growth
items.summary: Nirmal Jain said a Blackstone investment will let the shadow lender sustain 25% to 30% annual loan growth over three to four years, part of a wider surge in Indian non-bank lenders raising capital.

items.headline: India raises specialist police commando units to patrol its disputed border with China
items.summary: India has formed specialised commando units to patrol its contested Himalayan frontier with China, aiming to regain a tactical edge along the Line of Actual Control.

items.headline: Adani Ports agrees €2.56 billion deal to buy European storage operator Evos
items.summary: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone agreed to acquire European liquid-storage firm Evos in a deal valued at about €2.56 billion (US$2.9 billion) at enterprise level, expanding its overseas footprint.

items.headline: Burnham says Britain's 10-year plan will now be published before Christmas
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told the Commons his 10-year plan for Britain will be set out before the Christmas recess, reversing his earlier suggestion that it could slip into next year; it will include proposals for a national care service.

items.headline: Bank of England raises its key rate to 4%, its first hike in three years
items.summary: The Monetary Policy Committee voted 8-1 to lift the Bank Rate a quarter point to 4%, its first increase since 2023, and warned UK inflation could reach about 5% by mid-2027, citing Middle East energy costs.

items.headline: UK to require employers to publish salary ranges in job adverts
items.summary: The government will legislate to force pay ranges onto job advertisements, part of a push to narrow pay gaps and help people entering the workforce.

items.headline: Burnham pledges to overhaul benefit eligibility for young people
items.summary: As part of efforts to curb the welfare bill, Andy Burnham vowed to change benefit eligibility for young people while investing more in mental-health and employment support.

items.headline: Update: Russia and Ukraine agree a prisoner exchange as Abu Dhabi talks end without a territorial deal
items.summary: The latest round of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi closed with agreement on a large prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on territory or security guarantees, according to Al Jazeera, with envoys signalling further meetings.

items.headline: US Army officer arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
items.summary: British police arrested a 41-year-old field-grade US Army officer near Gloucester under the National Security Act 2023 over suspected Russian espionage; the Metropolitan Police called it a first-of-its-kind case and the Kremlin denied any involvement.

items.headline: At least eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza despite ceasefire
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported at least eight Palestinians, including a father and his 13-year-old son, were killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza; the territory's health ministry says more than 1,600 people have died since the October 2025 ceasefire took effect.

items.headline: Train collision near Cairo kills seven and injures more than 100
items.summary: A Giza-to-Fayoum train rear-ended a Cairo-Aswan service near al-Ayyat on 8 November, killing at least seven people, including a driver, and injuring more than 100; Egyptian authorities launched an investigation.

items.headline: Google unveils TPU 8tx and 8i Max AI chips, deepening its AMD partnership
items.summary: Google expanded its eighth-generation TPU line with the TPU 8tx, the first cloud TPU with hardware-enforced confidential computing and built on AMD EPYC host CPUs, and the memory-heavy TPU 8i Max for long-context inference.

items.headline: New York's frontier-AI safety law takes effect, adding oversight for OpenAI and Anthropic
items.summary: New York opened a registration portal under its RAISE Act, requiring large frontier-AI developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic to register by 1 January 2027, publish safety frameworks, and report critical incidents within 72 hours, with fines up to US$1 million per violation.

items.headline: Britain's Fractile reportedly raises about £540 million to challenge Nvidia in AI chips
items.summary: UK AI-chip startup Fractile has reportedly raised roughly £540 million (about US$720 million) in a Series C backed by Britain's Sovereign AI Fund, valuing it near US$6.5 billion, to accelerate its inference-focused silicon.

items.headline: Utah startup Torus raises US$500 million to pair batteries with AI computing
items.summary: Torus raised US$500 million in a Magnetar-led round to launch Foundry, a shipping-container-sized unit combining battery storage with AI compute, targeting power-constrained data-centre expansion.

items.headline: Wall Street rebounds as CoreWeave's earnings revive the AI trade
items.summary: US stocks rose on 11 November, with the Nasdaq gaining more than 1% as a sharp jump in CoreWeave and a rebound in Nvidia lifted the AI-infrastructure sector after a bruising stretch.

items.headline: CoreWeave soars on a strong third quarter and raised full-year guidance
items.summary: CoreWeave shares jumped after reporting third-quarter revenue of US$3.66 billion, up 168% year on year, and lifting its 2026 revenue outlook to US$13 billion to US$13.3 billion; chief executive Michael Intrator said he scrapped a planned share-sale programme.

items.headline: Fox raises US$8.4 billion in bonds to refinance its Roku acquisition
items.summary: Fox sold US$8.4 billion of investment-grade bonds to refinance its roughly US$22 billion purchase of Roku, drawing about US$39 billion of orders — nearly five times the offering.

items.headline: Vanguard raises US$4 billion in private debt to fund its Altruist deal
items.summary: Vanguard borrowed about US$4 billion in the private-placement market to finance its acquisition of digital wealth platform Altruist, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.headline: 🎾 Noskova stuns Gauff to become first into the WTA Finals semifinals
items.summary: Linda Noskova, the reigning Wimbledon champion, beat Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 at Indian Wells on 10 November to become the first player to reach the semifinals of the 2026 WTA Finals, on her tournament debut.

items.headline: 🎾 Rybakina withdraws from the WTA Finals but keeps the year-end No. 1 ranking
items.summary: World No. 1 Elena Rybakina pulled out of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells with a viral illness and was replaced by alternate Marta Kostyuk; she still finishes 2026 as the year-end No. 1.

items.headline: 🏏 Bangladesh salvage a draw but West Indies take the Test series 1-0
items.summary: Bad light ended the second Test in Sylhet in a draw, giving West Indies a 1-0 series win; Towhid Hridoy's unbeaten 242 and 82 set a Bangladesh Test record aggregate of 324, and Mushfiqur Rahim became the first Bangladeshi to pass 7,000 Test runs.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell expects a Las Vegas grid penalty for a new Mercedes engine
items.summary: George Russell said he is likely to take a second engine-change grid penalty at the Las Vegas Grand Prix on 21 November, by which time Mercedes team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli could already have the title sealed.

items.headline: Experimental brain gene therapy nearly eliminates seizures in epilepsy patients
items.summary: In a small early trial, three adults with drug-resistant epilepsy saw monthly seizures fall more than 90% after a gene-carrying virus was infused into the seizure focus, with the effect tunable via a low-dose drug and no serious side effects.

items.headline: Hundreds of 26,000-year-old engravings found hidden in a Spanish tourist cave
items.summary: Researchers reported 280 Palaeolithic motifs, including 55 animal figures, in Catalonia's Cova de la Font Major, a cave open to visitors since the 1990s, where the art had been obscured by graffiti and poor lighting.

items.headline: Independent method confirms the shadow of the M87 supermassive black hole
items.summary: A Nature study used a new interferometric technique to reproduce the ring-like shadow of M87*, measuring an angular diameter of about 42 microarcseconds and a mass near 6.5 billion suns, corroborating the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image.

items.headline: Study finds the first cancer-driver mutations usually arise in early adulthood
items.summary: A Nature study using deep sequencing of blood-cell clones in the years before acute myeloid leukaemia found that the first cancer-driving mutations typically emerge in early adulthood, while blood-cell populations are still highly diverse.

fun_fact.headline: Flamingos are born grey and turn pink only from their diet
fun_fact.body: Flamingos are not born pink — their chicks hatch grey. The rosy colour comes entirely from their diet: carotenoid pigments such as beta-carotene and canthaxanthin, absorbed from the algae and brine shrimp they eat. A flamingo kept on a carotenoid-free diet would slowly fade back to white.

puzzle.title: Twice the Length
puzzle.body:
Two candles are exactly the same length. Lit at the same moment, the first burns down completely in 4 hours and the second in 5 hours. Each burns at its own steady rate.

How long after lighting is one candle exactly twice as long as the other?
puzzle.approach: Write each candle's remaining length as a fraction of time, then set one equal to twice the other.
puzzle.answer:
3 hours 20 minutes (10/3 hours).

Let the original length be 1 and let t be the hours elapsed. The faster candle has length 1 − t/4; the slower one has length 1 − t/5, and is the longer of the two. Set the slower equal to twice the faster:
1 − t/5 = 2(1 − t/4)
1 − t/5 = 2 − t/2
t/2 − t/5 = 1  →  3t/10 = 1  →  t = 10/3.

At t = 10/3 h the candles measure 1/3 and 1/6 of their original length — exactly a 2:1 ratio.

word_puzzle.title: All That Glitters
word_puzzle.body:
Climb from SAND to GOLD in four steps. At each step change exactly one letter, keeping the other three, and every rung must be a real English word.

SAND → ____ → ____ → ____ → GOLD
word_puzzle.approach: Change exactly one letter at each step, and every rung must be an ordinary English word.
word_puzzle.answer:
SAND → BAND → BOND → BOLD → GOLD

Step 1  S→B  (SAND → BAND)
Step 2  A→O  (BAND → BOND)
Step 3  N→L  (BOND → BOLD)
Step 4  B→G  (BOLD → GOLD)

Four changes, one letter at a time, each rung a real word.
